High Court Of Andhra Pradesh
 At Amaravati
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition for the respondents.

2. This writ petition is filed questioning the action of the respondents in not paying land compensation to the subject land in an extent of Ac. 0.66 cents out of Ac.5.97 cents in R.S.No.483/3A,3B of I.S. Raghavapuram Village, Dwaraka Tirumala Mandal, West Godavari Miriyala Venkateswararao, vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58262936/
1 District which was acquired under SKKYR Project (Yerrakalava Project) prior to 2015.
3.

The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is the owner and the possessor of the subject land in an extent of Ac.0.66 cents out of Ac.5.97 cents in R.S.No.483/3A,3B of I.S.
Raghavapuram Village, Dwaraka Tirumala Mandal, West Godavari District.

While so, the said land was acquired along with the other extents of lands belonging to the others for the purpose of Yerrakalava Project under SKKYR Project Scheme prior to the year 2015 itself and no compensation was paid so far to the petitioner herein.

He further submits that the 3rd respondent also addressed a letter to the 5th respondent dated 03.08.2017 stating that the file was not traced in their office and it appears that the said file was transmitted to the office of the 5th respondent and sought for return of the file so as to take further action in the matter.

4. On the other hand, the learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition relying upon the counter of the respondents submits that as per the LP schedules submitted by the Irrigation Department, the petitioner is not notified as person interested either in Preliminary notification or Draft Declaration and the Award was passed in two spells of land acquisition for the lands in R.S.Nos. 483/3A, 3B to an extent of Ac.0.66 cents situated in I.S.Ragahavapuram Village, Dwaraka Tirumala Mandal.
The petitioner did not submit any objections under section 5A of the L.A. Act and did not submit any objection even at the time of award enquiry.
In this matter, awards were passed in the year 2005 and 2006.

The writ petitioner filed this writ petition in the year 2021 for the payment of compensation for the subject land even though the said land is not a part of L.P.
Schedule submitted by the Requisition department.
5. In view of the above said facts and circumstances, no relief for payment can be considered in this writ petition.

However, the petitioner is permitted to approach the 4th respondent by making a representation along with the necessary documents in support of his claim for payment of compensation for the subject land within a period of three (3) weeks from the date of receipt of this order.

On receipt of the same, the 4th respondent can consider the representation strictly in accordance with law and the same shall be disposed off as expeditiously as possible within a period of eight weeks thereafter by giving due opportunity to all the parties concerned including the petitioner and upon verification of the records and the subject land, appropriate decision shall be taken on it's own merits.
6. Accordingly, the writ petition is disposed off.
There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel, Miscellaneous Petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
JUSTICE B KRISHNA MOHAN 13.03.2024.
